questions.question: A magnetic field is produced around a conductor whenever:

options.A: Static electric charges reside on it
options.C: It is heated to high temperature

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (B) Electric current flows through it. Oersted discovered that moving electric charges (current) set up a concentric magnetic field around the conductor.

questions.question: The direction of magnetic field lines around a straight current-carrying wire is given by:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (A) Right-hand grip rule. Grasp the wire with the right hand so the thumb points in the direction of conventional current; the curled fingers show the direction of magnetic lines of force.

questions.question: The magnetic force F acting on a straight conductor of length L carrying current I in a uniform magnetic field B is:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (B) F = I (L × B). The magnetic deflecting force is given by F = ILB sinθ, which in vector form is F = I(L × B).

questions.question: The magnetic force on a current-carrying wire in a uniform magnetic field is maximum when the angle θ between wire and field is:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (B) 90°. Since F = ILB sinθ, maximum force occurs when sinθ = 1, i.e., θ = 90° (conductor perpendicular to field).

questions.question: The SI unit of magnetic flux density (magnetic field induction) B is:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (B) Tesla (T) or N A⁻¹ m⁻¹. 1 Tesla = 1 N / (A·m) = 1 Wb/m².

questions.question: Magnetic flux Φ_B through a planar area A in a uniform magnetic field B is given by:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (A) Φ_B = B · A = BA cosθ. Magnetic flux is the scalar dot product of magnetic flux density vector B and area vector A.

questions.question: The SI unit of magnetic flux Φ_B is:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (B) Weber (Wb) or N m A⁻¹. 1 Weber = 1 Tesla × 1 m² = 1 N·m/A = 1 V·s.

questions.question: Ampere's Circuital Law states that the line integral of B around any closed path enclosing current I is:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (A) ∮ B · dl = μ₀ I. Ampere's Law states that the sum of B·ΔL around a closed loop equals μ₀ times the total current enclosed.

questions.question: The value of permeability of free space μ₀ in SI units is:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (A) 4π × 10⁻⁷ T m A⁻¹. In vacuum, magnetic permeability constant μ₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ T·m/A (or H/m).

questions.question: The magnetic field B inside a long tightly wound solenoid with n turns per unit length carrying current I is:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (A) B = μ₀ n I. Inside an ideal solenoid, the field is uniform, strong, and parallel to the axis, with magnitude B = μ₀ n I = μ₀ (N/L) I.

questions.question: The magnetic force F acting on a charge q moving with velocity v in a magnetic field B is:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (B) F = q (v × B). The magnetic Lorentz force has magnitude F = qvB sinθ and acts perpendicular to both velocity and magnetic field.

questions.question: A charged particle moves parallel to the direction of a magnetic field. The magnetic force on it is:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (B) Zero. When moving parallel (θ = 0° or 180°), sinθ = 0, so magnetic force F = qvB sin 0° = 0.

questions.question: The total Lorentz force acting on a charge q moving in a region having both electric field E and magnetic field B is:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (A) F = q E + q (v × B). The Lorentz force equation combines both electrostatic and magnetic forces: F = F_e + F_m = q[E + (v × B)].

questions.question: Because the magnetic force F = q(v × B) is always perpendicular to velocity v, the work done by a magnetic force on a moving charge is:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (B) Zero. W = F · d = F · (v dt) = 0 because F ⊥ v. Hence a static magnetic field cannot change the kinetic energy or speed of a charge, only its direction.

questions.question: When a charged particle enters a uniform magnetic field perpendicularly, its path is a:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (B) Circle. The perpendicular magnetic force provides the required centripetal force: qvB = mv²/r, resulting in uniform circular motion of radius r = mv / (qB).

questions.question: In a velocity selector, electric and magnetic fields are arranged perpendicular to each other. Particles pass undeflected if velocity v equals:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (B) v = E / B. Equating electric force qE and magnetic force qvB gives qE = qvB, or v = E/B.

questions.question: In J.J. Thomson's experiment, the charge-to-mass ratio (e/m) of an electron is approximately:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (A) 1.7588 × 10¹¹ C kg⁻¹. Measured by J.J. Thomson in 1897, e/m = (1.602 × 10⁻¹⁹ C) / (9.109 × 10⁻³¹ kg) ≈ 1.76 × 10¹¹ C/kg.

questions.question: The torque τ on a planar coil of N turns, area A carrying current I in a magnetic field B making angle α with the plane of coil is:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (A) τ = NIAB cosα. If α is the angle between the coil plane and magnetic field, torque is τ = NIAB cosα (or τ = NIAB sinθ where θ is the angle with the coil normal).

questions.question: A galvanometer is converted into an ammeter of desired range by connecting a:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (B) Low resistance (shunt) in parallel. A tiny shunt resistance R_s = (I_g R_g) / (I - I_g) is connected in parallel so most current bypasses the delicate galvanometer coil.

questions.question: The value of shunt resistance R_s required to convert a galvanometer into an ammeter of full scale deflection I is:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (A) R_s = I_g R_g / (I - I_g). Potential drop across shunt equals drop across galvanometer: (I - I_g) R_s = I_g R_g.

questions.question: A galvanometer is converted into a voltmeter of desired range V by connecting a:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (B) High resistance in series. Connecting a high resistance R_h = (V / I_g) - R_g in series limits current to I_g at full-scale voltage V.

questions.question: The value of high multiplier resistance R_h required to convert a galvanometer into a voltmeter of range V is:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (A) R_h = (V / I_g) - R_g. Total voltage V = I_g (R_g + R_h), hence R_h = (V/I_g) - R_g.

questions.question: An ideal ammeter has an internal resistance of:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (A) Zero. An ideal ammeter inserted in series should introduce zero additional resistance to avoid disturbing circuit current.

questions.question: An ideal voltmeter has an internal resistance of:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (B) Infinite. An ideal voltmeter connected in parallel across a component should draw zero current so it does not alter potential drop.

questions.question: In a moving coil galvanometer, a radial magnetic field is produced by using:

options.A: Concave pole pieces and a soft iron cylinder

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (A) Concave pole pieces and a soft iron cylinder. Cylindrical concave pole pieces with a central soft-iron core ensure field lines are always radial, making the deflecting torque constant (cosα = 1) and scale linear.

questions.question: Two parallel conductors carrying currents in the SAME direction:

options.C: Exert no force on each other
options.D: Rotate each other without translational force

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (B) Attract each other. According to Ampere's force law, parallel currents in the same direction attract, whereas antiparallel currents repel.

questions.question: The magnetic dipole moment M of a current-carrying loop of area A with N turns carrying current I is:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (A) M = N I A. Magnetic dipole moment is defined as M = NIA with unit A·m² (or J/T).

questions.question: In an ohmmeter, the scale is:

options.A: Linear with zero at left end
options.B: Non-linear with zero at right end and infinity at left end
options.C: Linear with infinity at right end

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (B) Non-linear with zero at right end and infinity at left end. Full deflection current corresponds to zero external resistance (R_x = 0), and zero deflection corresponds to open circuit (R_x = ∞).

questions.question: An AVO meter (multimeter) can measure:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (A) Amperes, Volts, and Ohms. AVO stands for Amperes (current), Volts (potential difference), and Ohms (resistance).

questions.question: The radius r of the circular path of an electron in a magnetic field B with momentum p = mv is:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (A) r = mv / (qB) = p / (eB). Equating centripetal force mv²/r to magnetic force evB gives r = mv / (eB).

questions.question: The time period T of circular revolution of a charged particle in a magnetic field is:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (A) T = 2πm / (qB). Period T = 2πr/v = 2π(mv/qB)/v = 2πm/(qB), which is remarkably independent of velocity and radius (cyclotron principle).

questions.question: A digital multimeter (DMM) displays measurements digitally using an analog-to-digital converter (ADC) and offers:

options.B: High input impedance and elimination of parallax errors
options.C: Higher loading effect than moving coil meters

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (B) High input impedance and elimination of parallax errors. DMMs provide direct numerical readouts, avoiding parallax, and feature very high input resistance (~10 MΩ) to prevent circuit loading.

questions.question: A proton and an electron enter a magnetic field with the same velocity perpendicular to the field. The radius of curvature of the proton will be:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (B) Much larger than electron (~1836 times). Since r = mv/(qB) and q and v are equal, r ∝ m. Since m_p ≈ 1836 m_e, r_p is ~1836 times larger.

questions.question: Current sensitivity of a galvanometer is defined as the deflection θ produced per unit current (θ / I). It is equal to:
questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (A) NAB / C. In equilibrium, restoring torque Cθ equals deflecting torque NIAB, giving θ/I = NAB/C, where C is the torsional couple per unit twist.

questions.question: To increase the sensitivity of a galvanometer, one should:

options.A: Increase torsional constant C of suspension wire
options.C: Use a suspension wire with small torsional constant C (phosphor-bronze)

questions.explanation: Correct Answer: (C) Use a suspension wire with small torsional constant C (phosphor-bronze). Since sensitivity S = NAB/C, reducing C (using phosphor-bronze hairspring or suspension) substantially increases sensitivity.
